newsitem.title: USA: AT&T chairman confides co needs partner - NYT.
newsitem.headline: AT&T chairman confides co needs partner - NYT.

text.p: AT&T Corp Chairman Robert Allen has said that the telecommunications giant needs a local telephone partner and that his designated heir doesn't need to run the combined company, the New York Times said.
In Thursday's edition, the Times said those admissions came in the midst of merger talks with SBC Communications Inc, the largest provider of local telephone service in the United States.
The Times quoted unnamed sources familiar with the talks as saying Allen has confided that AT&T needs a local telephone partner to compete in a deregulated market.

Allen also reportedly has said that his heir apparent at AT&T, President John Walter, would not necessarily need to run the combined company. Some news reports have suggested that SBC Chairman Edward Whitacre would take over the reins of a combined company.
If consummated, the merger of the two companies would create the world's largest phone company. The deal is worth a potential $50 billion, according to some reports.
